selftest.answer: It takes me ten minutes instead of thirty.
selftest.why_en: The other two say the same claim again in new words.

lesson.arabic-formal-email.title_en: A formal email: أَرْجُو, مُرْفَق, شُكْرًا مُسْبَقًا
lesson.arabic-formal-email.family_en: Opening, the request, attachments and closing, politely and clearly

table.en: I have a question about the course

steps: A formal email says who it's for, why you're writing, what they need to know, and exactly what you're asking.
Open with the person's title and الْمُحْتَرَمُ, then a greeting: تَحِيَّةً طَيِّبَةً.
Make the request plain. أَرْجُو, I'd be grateful for, is followed by what you ask for, usually as a verbal noun: أَرْجُو إِرْسَالَ الْفَاتُورَةِ, please send the invoice.
To an office, or someone you don't know, use the plural "you": تَجِدُونَ, you will find.
Check names, dates and attachments before sending, and close with شُكْرًا مُسْبَقًا, thank you in advance.

examples.ar: أَكْتُبُ إِلَيْكُمْ بِخُصُوصِ التَّسْجِيلِ فِي الدَّوْرَةِ.
examples.en: I'm writing to you about registering for the course.

examples.ar: أَرْجُو إِرْسَالَ الْبَرْنَامَجِ قَبْلَ يَوْمِ الْخَمِيسِ.
examples.en: Please send the programme before Thursday.
Please find the certificate attached to this email.

why.q_en: Why أَرْجُو إِرْسَالَ, with a noun, and not أَرْجُو أَنْ تُرْسِلُوا?
why.a_en: Both are right. أَرْجُو أَنْ تُرْسِلُوا uses أَنْ and a verb; أَرْجُو إِرْسَالَ uses the verbal noun, which sounds more formal and suits an email to an office.

selftest.q_en: How do you say "thank you in advance"?
selftest.why_en: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا is "thank you very much", and عَفْوًا "you're welcome".

selftest.q_en: What does مُرْفَق mean?
selftest.why_en: مُرْفَق describes a file or a photo sent with the email; the plural is مُرْفَقَات, attachments.

selftest.q_en: Writing to an office, how do you say "you will find"?
selftest.why_en: The plural "you" is the polite one in a formal email. تَجِدُ is to one man, and تَجِدِينَ to one woman.

lesson.arabic-summary-notes.title_en: Summarising: who said what, in fewer words
lesson.arabic-summary-notes.family_en: Reporting a source's points faithfully, and keeping your view apart
steps: A summary keeps the main points, and their limits, in fewer words.
Say whose point it is: يَرَى الْكَاتِبُ أَنَّ, the writer thinks that; أَشَارَ إِلَى, pointed to; أَضَافَ أَنَّ, added that.
قَدْ before a present verb means "may": قَدْ يُسَاعِدُ, it may help. Keep it, or you make the source sound surer than it is.
Notes can be fragments; the summary needs full sentences with clear links between them.
Keep your own view out of the source's points. If you add it, put it in its own sentence, starting فِي رَأْيِي.

examples.ar: أَشَارَ الْكَاتِبُ إِلَى أَنَّ الْمَشْرُوعَ قَدْ يُسَاعِدُ بَعْضَ الطُّلَّابِ.
examples.en: The writer pointed out that the project may help some students.

examples.ar: أَضَافَ أَنَّ النَّتَائِجَ مَا زَالَتْ أَوَّلِيَّةً.
examples.en: He added that the results are still preliminary.

examples.ar: بِشَكْلٍ عَامٍّ، تَدْعُو الْمَقَالَةُ إِلَى الصَّبْرِ.
examples.en: Overall, the article calls for patience.

why.q_en: Why أَشَارَ إِلَى أَنَّ, with both إِلَى and أَنَّ?
why.a_en: أَشَارَ takes إِلَى before what it points to. When that's a whole statement, أَنَّ brings it in: أَشَارَ إِلَى أَنَّ الْمَشْرُوعَ مُفِيدٌ, he pointed out that the project is useful.

selftest.q_en: The source says قَدْ يُسَاعِدُ. Which summary keeps its meaning?
selftest.why_en: قَدْ with a present verb is "may": keep the limit.

selftest.q_en: What does أَضَافَ mean?
selftest.why_en: "He summarised" is لَخَّصَ.

selftest.q_en: Where does your own opinion go?
choices: in a separate sentence, marked as yours
selftest.answer: in a separate sentence, marked as yours
selftest.why_en: Keep the source's account and your view apart.

lesson.arabic-orthography-editing.title_en: Checking your spelling: ة, ى and where a hamza sits
lesson.arabic-orthography-editing.family_en: The letters learners mix up, the hamza's seat, and Arabic punctuation

table.en: the "tied t" at the end of a word
the "shortened alif": written short, said as a long ā at the end of a word

steps: Edit in passes: first the meaning and the order, then one spelling pattern at a time.
ة, the تَاءٌ مَرْبُوطَةٌ, ends a feminine noun and is said -a, or -at- before an ending: مَدِينَة, مَدِينَتُنَا. A plain ه is a real h: وَجْه, a face.
ى at the end, the أَلِفٌ مَقْصُورَةٌ, is a long ā: عَلَى, مُسْتَشْفَى. ي, with its dots, is ī or y: فِي.
At the end of a word, a hamza sits on the letter that matches the vowel before it: بَدَأَ after a, شَاطِئ after i, تَبَاطُؤ after u. After a sukūn or a long vowel it stands alone: جُزْء, سَمَاء.
Arabic's comma and question mark face the other way. Use them to help the reader, not to patch an unclear sentence.

examples.en: The lesson started on time.

words.en: started (hamza on an alif: a before it)

examples.en: We sat on the beach until the evening.

words.en: the beach (hamza on a ي-shape: i before it)

examples.en: Have you read the first part?

words.en: the part (hamza alone: a sukūn before it)

why.q_en: Why شَاطِئ, with the hamza on a ي-shape, but بَدَأَ with it on an alif?
why.a_en: The seat follows the vowel before the hamza: i before it in شَاطِئ, so a ي-shaped seat; a before it in بَدَأَ, so an alif.

selftest.q_en: Which letter writes the feminine ending of مَدِينَة?
selftest.why_en: ة is the تَاءٌ مَرْبُوطَةٌ. A plain ه is a real h.

selftest.q_en: Where does the hamza sit in بَدَأَ?
selftest.why_en: The vowel before it is a.

selftest.q_en: What is a فَاصِلَة?
selftest.why_en: A question mark is عَلَامَةُ الِاسْتِفْهَامِ.

lesson.arabic-feedback-rewrite.family_en: The words for drafts and corrections, and how to make feedback stick
steps: Feedback helps when you understand a correction well enough to use it in a new sentence.
Sort the comments: meaning, order, grammar, spelling. Fix the meaning first.
Pick two or three patterns that keep coming back, rather than changing every sentence at once.
Grammar comments often name a word's gender: مُذَكَّر, masculine, or مُؤَنَّث, feminine. Words that describe it, or point to it, must match.
Keep your first مُسَوَّدَة, so you can see what changed and why.

examples.en: The teacher corrected the mistakes in my draft.

examples.ar: أَعَدْتُ كِتَابَةَ الْفِقْرَةِ بَعْدَ قِرَاءَةِ التَّعْلِيقَاتِ.
examples.en: I rewrote the paragraph after reading the comments.

examples.ar: تَحَسَّنَتْ كِتَابَتِي كَثِيرًا فِي الشَّهْرِ الْأَخِيرِ.
examples.en: My writing has improved a lot in the last month.

why.q_en: Why أَعَدْتُ, with a short a, from أَعَادَ?
why.a_en: أَعَادَ has a long ā in the middle, and, as in قَالَ, قُلْتُ, it shortens before an ending that starts with a consonant. Here the short vowel stays a: أَعَدْتُ, I did again.

selftest.q_en: What is a مُسَوَّدَة?
selftest.why_en: A comment is تَعْلِيق.

selftest.q_en: What does مُؤَنَّث mean?
selftest.why_en: Masculine is مُذَكَّر.

selftest.q_en: You get twenty comments. What do you do first?
choices: fix the meaning, then two or three repeated patterns
selftest.answer: fix the meaning, then two or three repeated patterns
selftest.why_en: A few patterns you understand do more than many changes you don't.

lesson.arabic-b1-source-task.title_en: Comparing two sources: يَتَّفِقُ, يَخْتَلِفُ, مُشْتَرَك
lesson.arabic-b1-source-task.family_en: Keeping each source's points apart, then saying where they meet and part
steps: Keep each source's points apart first: its topic, its main point, and its evidence.
Then compare: يَتَّفِقُ النَّصَّانِ عَلَى, the two texts agree on; يَخْتَلِفُ النَّصَّانِ فِي, the two texts differ on.
A shared topic isn't a shared claim: two texts about learning can answer different questions.
غَيْر, not, turns a describing word round, and the word after it takes -i, here -in: غَيْرُ مَوْثُوقٍ, unreliable.
Two sources agreeing doesn't make a claim true: it shows only that they agree.

examples.en: The two writers agree on the importance of reading.
But they differ on the reasons.
This website isn't reliable.

why.q_en: Why يَتَّفِقُ الْكَاتِبَانِ, singular, but لَكِنَّهُمَا يَخْتَلِفَانِ, for two?
why.a_en: A verb that comes before its doers stays singular, even for two or more: يَتَّفِقُ الْكَاتِبَانِ. When the doers come first, as a noun or a pronoun, the verb matches them: لَكِنَّهُمَا يَخْتَلِفَانِ, but they two differ.

selftest.q_en: What does مُشْتَرَك mean?
selftest.why_en: مَوْضُوعٌ مُشْتَرَكٌ is a shared topic.

selftest.q_en: How do you say "unreliable"?
selftest.why_en: غَيْر comes before the describing word, which ends in -in. لَيْسَ would need -an (لَيْسَ مَوْثُوقًا, it isn't reliable), and لَا doesn't make a describing word negative this way.

selftest.q_en: What does قَارَنَ بَيْنَ mean?
selftest.why_en: قَارَنَ بَيْنَ النَّصَّيْنِ: he compared the two texts.

lesson.arabic-b1-explainer.title_en: Explaining something to a listener: شَرَحَ, وَحْدَهُ لَا يَكْفِي
lesson.arabic-b1-explainer.family_en: The question first, a simple example, links between points, and a check

table.en: on its own, it isn't enough

steps: Start with the question you're answering, so the listener knows where you're going.
Bring in only the terms they need, and explain each one simply.
Give one concrete example that supports the point.
Link your points so each builds on the last: وَحْدَهُ لَا يَكْفِي, on its own it isn't enough; أَيْضًا, also.
Check with هَلْ هَذَا وَاضِحٌ؟, then close with فِي الْخِتَامِ and the point in one sentence.

examples.ar: الْحِفْظُ وَحْدَهُ لَا يَكْفِي لِتَعَلُّمِ لُغَةٍ.
examples.en: Memorising alone isn't enough to learn a language.
The teacher explained the rule with a simple example.

examples.ar: فِي الْخِتَامِ، الِاسْتِعْمَالُ هُوَ أَفْضَلُ طَرِيقَةٍ لِلتَّعَلُّمِ.
examples.en: In closing, using the language is the best way to learn.

why.q_en: Why وَحْدَهُ in الْحِفْظُ وَحْدَهُ, but وَحْدَهَا for reading?
why.a_en: وَحْدَ, alone, always carries an ending for whoever or whatever is alone: وَحْدِي, on my own; وَحْدَهُ for a masculine word; وَحْدَهَا for a feminine one. The verb matches too: الْقِرَاءَةُ وَحْدَهَا لَا تَكْفِي.

selftest.q_en: How do you check your listener has followed?
selftest.why_en: فِي الْخِتَامِ closes, and وَحْدَهُ لَا يَكْفِي links a point.

selftest.q_en: Which says "Reading alone isn't enough"?
selftest.why_en: قِرَاءَة is feminine, so وَحْدَهَا and تَكْفِي.

selftest.q_en: What should an explanation start with?
selftest.why_en: Then the listener knows where you're heading.

lesson.arabic-b1-unprepared.title_en: Answering on the spot: دَعْنِي أُفَكِّرُ, يَعْتَمِدُ عَلَى
lesson.arabic-b1-unprepared.family_en: Taking a moment, saying how sure you are, and answering the question asked
steps: Listen for what the question actually asks: لِمَاذَا wants a reason, not a name.
It's fine to take a moment: دَعْنِي أُفَكِّرُ, let me think.
Say how sure you are, or how you mean it: عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي, as far as I know; فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ, actually; بِصَرَاحَةٍ, honestly.
If the answer depends on something, say so with يَعْتَمِدُ عَلَى, it depends on.
If you're unsure what's being asked, check before you answer: a fluent answer to the wrong question doesn't help.

examples.en: Let me think for a moment.

examples.ar: اِخْتَرْتُ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ لِأَنَّ قِصَّتَهُ تُشْبِهُ حَيَاتِي.
examples.en: I chose this book because its story is like my own life.

examples.ar: عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي، تَبْدَأُ الْمُحَاضَرَةُ فِي التَّاسِعَةِ.
examples.en: As far as I know, the lecture starts at nine.

words.en: my knowledge: "as far as I know"

why.q_en: Why اِخْتَرْتُ, with a short a, from اِخْتَارَ?
why.a_en: The long ā in the middle shortens before an ending that starts with a consonant, as in قَالَ, قُلْتُ: اِخْتَارَ, he chose; اِخْتَرْتُ, I chose.

selftest.q_en: Which phrase gives you a moment to think?
selftest.why_en: عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي is "as far as I know", and بِصَرَاحَةٍ "honestly".

selftest.q_en: What does يَعْتَمِدُ عَلَى mean?
selftest.why_en: هَذَا يَعْتَمِدُ عَلَى الْوَقْتِ: that depends on the time.

selftest.q_en: You're asked لِمَاذَا اخْتَرْتَ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ؟ What does the answer need?
selftest.why_en: لِمَاذَا asks why.

lesson.arabic-b1-independent-cycle.title_en: Planning your own learning: أَوْلَوِيَّة, تَمْرِين, تَدْرِيجِيًّا
lesson.arabic-b1-independent-cycle.family_en: A small cycle you can repeat: choose, practise, check, record
steps: A learning cycle has four steps: choose a text you can mostly follow, find a few gaps, practise them, then check them in something new.
Give a small set of gaps أَوْلَوِيَّة, priority: ones you can fix now, not everything at once.
Practise them with a short تَمْرِين, and keep a سِجِلّ of what you did and what help you used.
Raise the difficulty تَدْرِيجِيًّا, gradually. Easy texts still count.

examples.ar: أَوْلَوِيَّتِي هَذَا الشَّهْرَ كَلِمَاتُ السَّبَبِ وَالنَّتِيجَةِ.
examples.en: My priority this month is the words for cause and result.

examples.ar: أَكْتُبُ فِي سِجِلِّي مَا تَعَلَّمْتُهُ كُلَّ أُسْبُوعٍ.
examples.en: Every week I write down in my log what I learned.
Learning takes patience.

why.q_en: Why تَدْرِيجِيًّا, with -an?
why.a_en: تَدْرِيجِيّ means gradual. Used to say how something is done, it takes -an, like كَثِيرًا and جِدًّا: أَتَقَدَّمُ تَدْرِيجِيًّا, I'm making progress gradually.

selftest.q_en: What is a سِجِلّ?
selftest.why_en: A priority is أَوْلَوِيَّة.

selftest.q_en: What does تَدْرِيجِيًّا mean?
selftest.why_en: "Daily" is يَوْمِيًّا.

selftest.q_en: What is a تَمْرِين?
selftest.why_en: A record is سِجِلّ, and patience صَبْر.

lesson.arabic-b1-portfolio.title_en: Describing what you can do: قَادِرٌ عَلَى, نُقْطَةُ قُوَّةٍ, دَلِيل
lesson.arabic-b1-portfolio.family_en: Saying what you can do, with the evidence and the help you had
steps: Say what you can do, with evidence: أَنَا قَادِرٌ عَلَى شَرْحِ فِكْرَةٍ بَسِيطَةٍ, I can explain a simple idea. A woman says قَادِرَةٌ.
قَادِرٌ عَلَى takes a noun, often a verbal noun: قَادِرٌ عَلَى الْكِتَابَةِ, able to write.
Give each piece of دَلِيل, evidence, its date and the help you had. Was it مُسْتَقِلّ, done on your own?
Choose your next مَرْحَلَة from your skills as they really are: a تَخَصُّص, a specialism, builds on the common ones.

examples.en: My strong point is reading.
I've become able to understand the news. (a woman)
This recording is evidence of my progress.

why.q_en: Why قَادِرٌ عَلَى الْكِتَابَةِ, with a noun, where English says "able to write"?
why.a_en: عَلَى is followed by a noun, so the action becomes a verbal noun: الْكِتَابَة, writing. You can also use أَنْ and a verb: قَادِرٌ عَلَى أَنْ أَكْتُبَ.

selftest.q_en: How does a woman say "I'm able to explain"?
selftest.why_en: A woman adds ـَة, and قَادِر takes عَلَى.

selftest.q_en: What is نُقْطَةُ قُوَّةٍ?
selftest.why_en: قُوَّة is strength.

selftest.q_en: What should each piece of evidence say?
choices: its date and the help you had
nothing: the work speaks for itself
selftest.answer: its date and the help you had
selftest.why_en: Then it shows what you can do, and under what conditions.

phrases_ar: أَنَا قَادِرٌ عَلَى شَرْحِ فِكْرَةٍ بَسِيطَةٍ

lesson.arabic-headlines-leads.title_en: Reading headlines: a verbal noun, and what it leaves out
lesson.arabic-headlines-leads.family_en: How headlines save words, and the words for the people who write the news

table.form_en: a verbal noun as a headline

steps: Headlines save words. They often use a verbal noun instead of a verb, and leave out who, when and where: اِفْتِتَاحُ مَعْرِضٍ لِلْكِتَابِ, opening of a book fair.
Read a headline as the promise of a story: the first paragraph usually fills in who, where and when.
Don't fill a gap yourself. If the report names no one, it may say only جِهَةٌ رَسْمِيَّةٌ, an official body.
Tell a stated fact from a question or someone's claim: a headline in quotation marks reports what someone said.

examples.en: An accident on the motorway (literally "the happening of an accident").

examples.ar: قَالَ مُرَاسِلُ الصَّحِيفَةِ إِنَّ الْحَادِثَ وَقَعَ صَبَاحًا.
examples.en: The newspaper's correspondent said the accident happened in the morning.

examples.ar: شَارَكَ فِي الْمَعْرِضِ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ مِئَةِ دَارِ نَشْرٍ.
examples.en: More than a hundred publishers took part in the fair.

why.q_en: Why اِفْتِتَاحُ, a noun, and not the verb اِفْتَتَحَ, in a headline?
why.a_en: A verbal noun names the event without saying who did it or when, which saves words. The report under the headline adds what the noun leaves out.

selftest.q_en: The headline says وُقُوعُ حَادِثٍ. What does it tell you?
selftest.why_en: The verbal noun names the event only. The report adds the rest.

selftest.q_en: What is a مُرَاسِل?
selftest.why_en: A newspaper is صَحِيفَة, and a participant مُشَارِك.

selftest.q_en: What is خَبَرٌ عَاجِلٌ?
selftest.why_en: عَاجِل is urgent.

lesson.arabic-news-language.title_en: Who says so: news verbs (أَعْلَنَ, أَفَادَ, نَفَى) and the passive
lesson.arabic-news-language.family_en: Verbs that say where a claim comes from, and how strongly
steps: News says who a claim comes from, and each verb has its own strength: أَعْلَنَ, announced, officially; أَفَادَ, stated; رَجَّحَ, thought likely; نَفَى, denied.
بِحَسَبِ, according to, names the source of a claim: بِحَسَبِ الْوِزَارَةِ, according to the ministry.
The passive leaves out who did it: يُرَجَّحُ, it's thought likely; أُعْلِنَ, it was announced. Don't add a doer the text doesn't give.
In a summary, keep the verb's strength: "announced" and "thought likely" aren't the same.

examples.en: The council announced the opening of a public park.
The official denied there was any delay.

examples.ar: يُرَجَّحُ أَنْ تَنْتَهِيَ الْأَعْمَالُ فِي الصَّيْفِ.
examples.en: The work is expected to finish in the summer.

why.q_en: Why يُرَجَّحُ, with u and a, and not يُرَجِّحُ?
why.a_en: The vowels make it passive. يُرَجِّحُ is "he thinks it likely"; يُرَجَّحُ is "it's thought likely", with no one named. Without the marks the two look the same, so the sentence decides.

selftest.q_en: Which verb means "denied"?
selftest.why_en: The other two report what someone said: "announced" and "stated".

selftest.q_en: What does مَصَادِرُ مُطَّلِعَةٌ mean?
selftest.why_en: مَصَادِر are sources, and مُطَّلِع someone who knows the inside story.

selftest.q_en: Which is the passive, "it was announced"?
selftest.why_en: أَعْلَنَ is "he announced", and أَعْلِنْ "announce!".

lesson.arabic-numbers-data.title_en: Numbers in the news: اِرْتَفَعَ, اِنْخَفَضَ, فِي الْمِئَةِ
lesson.arabic-numbers-data.family_en: Rises and falls, rates and averages, and what a figure needs to mean anything
steps: A figure means little without its unit, its starting point and its period: rose to what, from what, since when?
اِرْتَفَعَ, rose, and اِنْخَفَضَ, fell, take مِنْ for the start and إِلَى for the end: اِرْتَفَعَ عَدَدُ الطُّلَّابِ مِنْ خَمْسِينَ إِلَى سِتِّينَ.
"Per cent" is فِي الْمِئَةِ, "in the hundred". A rate going from 40 to 50 per cent rises by ten points, but by a quarter of what it was.
ضِعْف is double: ضِعْفُ الْعَدَدِ, twice the number. مُتَوَسِّط is an average.
Write an important figure down, with its unit, before you interpret it.

examples.ar: اِرْتَفَعَ عَدَدُ الزُّوَّارِ إِلَى مِلْيُونٍ هَذَا الْعَامَ.
examples.en: The number of visitors rose to a million this year.

examples.ar: اِنْخَفَضَتْ نِسْبَةُ الْبِطَالَةِ إِلَى سَبْعَةٍ فِي الْمِئَةِ.
examples.en: The unemployment rate fell to seven per cent.

examples.ar: بَلَغَ مُتَوَسِّطُ الْأَسْعَارِ ضِعْفَ مَا كَانَ عَلَيْهِ.
examples.en: Average prices reached double what they were.

why.q_en: Why اِنْخَفَضَتْ, with ـَتْ, in اِنْخَفَضَتْ نِسْبَةُ الْبِطَالَةِ?
why.a_en: When the verb comes first, it matches the gender of its subject, the noun right after it: نِسْبَة is feminine, so اِنْخَفَضَتْ. With عَدَد, masculine, it's اِنْخَفَضَ الْعَدَدُ.

selftest.q_en: What does اِنْخَفَضَ mean?
selftest.why_en: "Rose" is اِرْتَفَعَ.

selftest.q_en: How do you say "ten per cent"?
selftest.why_en: "Per cent" is فِي الْمِئَةِ, "in the hundred".

selftest.q_en: A rate goes from 40 to 50 per cent. By how many points did it rise?
selftest.why_en: Ten points; as a share of where it started, that's a rise of a quarter.

phrases_ar: اِرْتَفَعَ عَدَدُ الطُّلَّابِ مِنْ خَمْسِينَ إِلَى سِتِّينَ

lesson.arabic-interview-notes.title_en: Notes from an interview: who said what, and how sure
lesson.arabic-interview-notes.family_en: The words for an interview, and how to note a claim with its limits
steps: Keep three things apart in your notes: the question, the guest's answer, and your own reading of it.
Note a claim with its example and any limit the guest puts on it: "in my experience" belongs beside the claim.
Keep "not yet" as "not yet": لَمْ يَصِلِ الضَّيْفُ بَعْدُ, the guest hasn't arrived yet, isn't "he isn't coming".
A quotation, اِقْتِبَاس, must be the exact words: check its صِيَاغَة, wording, against the recording.
If the guest dodges a question, note that it wasn't answered, not what you guess the answer was.

examples.ar: سَأَلَ الْمُحَاوِرُ الضَّيْفَ عَنْ مَوْقِفِهِ مِنَ الْقَرَارِ.
examples.en: The interviewer asked the guest about his position on the decision.

examples.ar: قَالَ الضَّيْفُ إِنَّ الْفِكْرَةَ نَجَحَتْ فِي تَجْرِبَتِهِ الشَّخْصِيَّةِ.
examples.en: The guest said the idea had worked in his own experience.
The guest dodged the second question.

why.q_en: Why مِنْ after تَهَرَّبَ?
why.a_en: تَهَرَّبَ means to dodge or slip away, and like هَرَبَ, to escape, it takes مِنْ before what you avoid: تَهَرَّبَ مِنَ السُّؤَالِ, he dodged the question.

selftest.q_en: Who is the مُحَاوِر?
selftest.why_en: The guest is the ضَيْف.

selftest.q_en: What is an اِقْتِبَاس?
selftest.why_en: A quotation must keep the exact words.

selftest.q_en: The guest says "in my experience". Where does that go in your notes?
selftest.why_en: Without it, a personal view can look like a general one.

lesson.arabic-news-digest.title_en: A news digest: keeping sources, dates and doubts
lesson.arabic-news-digest.family_en: Words for updates, conflicting accounts and what isn't confirmed

table.en: as he put it, in his words

steps: A digest picks the main points from several sources and groups them by topic, not source by source.
Keep each point's source and date: a later تَحْدِيث, update, may change an earlier report.
Where sources disagree, keep both: رِوَايَاتٌ مُتَنَاقِضَةٌ, conflicting accounts.
Mark what isn't settled: غَيْرُ مُؤَكَّدٍ, unconfirmed; عَلَى حَدِّ قَوْلِهِ, as he put it.
Link the points in your own words rather than pasting sentences.

examples.ar: أَفَادَ التَّحْدِيثُ الْأَخِيرُ بِأَنَّ الطَّرِيقَ مَفْتُوحٌ.
examples.en: The latest update said the road is open.

examples.ar: مَا زَالَ عَدَدُ الْمُشَارِكِينَ غَيْرَ مُؤَكَّدٍ.
examples.en: The number of participants is still unconfirmed.

examples.ar: اِرْتَفَعَتِ الْأَسْعَارُ بِالْمُقَارَنَةِ مَعَ الْعَامِ الْمَاضِي.
examples.en: Prices rose compared with last year.

why.q_en: Why غَيْرَ, with -a, in مَا زَالَ عَدَدُ الْمُشَارِكِينَ غَيْرَ مُؤَكَّدٍ?
why.a_en: مَا زَالَ is a sister of كَانَ, so the describing part takes -a. Here that part is غَيْرُ مُؤَكَّدٍ, so غَيْر takes the -a, and مُؤَكَّد keeps the -in it always has after غَيْر.

selftest.q_en: What is a تَحْدِيث?
selftest.why_en: A later update may change an earlier report.

selftest.q_en: What does عَلَى حَدِّ قَوْلِهِ show?
choices: that these are his words, not the writer's
selftest.answer: that these are his words, not the writer's
selftest.why_en: It keeps the claim with the person who made it.

selftest.q_en: What is نَشْرَةُ الْأَخْبَارِ?
selftest.why_en: A newspaper is صَحِيفَة.

lesson.arabic-claim-evidence.title_en: Claims and evidence: اِدِّعَاء, دَلِيلٌ كَافٍ, تَعْمِيم
lesson.arabic-claim-evidence.family_en: What a writer claims, what supports it, and when one example becomes a generalisation

table.en: an argument, a reason offered as proof
he supported his view with an example

steps: A claim, اِدِّعَاء, is what the writer wants you to accept; evidence is what's offered to support it.
Test the evidence three ways: is it ذُو صِلَةٍ, relevant? Is it كَافٍ, enough? Does it cover more than one case?
One example can illustrate; turning it into a rule for everyone is a تَعْمِيم, a generalisation.
Keep apart whether you agree with the conclusion and how well it's supported.
ذُو, "having", changes with its noun's ending: دَلِيلٌ ذُو صِلَةٍ, but دَلِيلًا ذَا صِلَةٍ and بِدَلِيلٍ ذِي صِلَةٍ.

examples.ar: دَعَمَ الْكَاتِبُ رَأْيَهُ بِأَرْقَامٍ مِنْ ثَلَاثِ دِرَاسَاتٍ.
examples.en: The writer supported his view with figures from three studies.

examples.ar: هَذَا الْمِثَالُ وَحْدَهُ لَيْسَ دَلِيلًا كَافِيًا.
examples.en: This example alone isn't sufficient evidence.

examples.ar: الْحُجَّةُ مُقْنِعَةٌ، لَكِنَّهَا تَقُومُ عَلَى تَعْمِيمٍ.
examples.en: The argument is convincing, but it rests on a generalisation.

why.q_en: Why كَافٍ in دَلِيلٌ كَافٍ, but كَافِيًا in لَيْسَ دَلِيلًا كَافِيًا?
why.a_en: Words like كَافٍ end in a long ī that drops with -un and -in: كَافٍ. With -an the ي stays: كَافِيًا. It's the same with غَالٍ, غَالِيًا.

selftest.q_en: What is a تَعْمِيم?
selftest.why_en: It turns one or a few cases into a rule for all.

selftest.q_en: Which says "relevant evidence"?
selftest.why_en: دَلِيلٌ ends in -un, so ذُو. ذَا goes with -an, and ذِي with -in.

selftest.q_en: What does مُقْنِع mean?
selftest.why_en: "Relevant" is ذُو صِلَةٍ, and "sufficient" كَافٍ.

lesson.arabic-stance-hedging.title_en: How sure a claim is: بِالتَّأْكِيدِ, عَلَى الْأَرْجَحِ, يَبْدُو أَنَّ
lesson.arabic-stance-hedging.family_en: Words that set the strength of a claim, from certain to possible
steps: These words set how sure a claim is. They aren't decoration: change one and you change the claim.
From surest to least sure: بِالتَّأْكِيدِ, certainly; عَلَى الْأَرْجَحِ, most likely; مِنَ الْمُحْتَمَلِ أَنْ, it's likely that; رُبَّمَا, perhaps; لَا أَسْتَبْعِدُ, I don't rule it out.
Watch what follows: مِنَ الْمُحْتَمَلِ أَنْ takes a present verb ending in -a; يَبْدُو أَنَّ takes a noun ending in -a.
قَدْ with a present verb is "may": قَدْ يَتَأَخَّرُ الْقِطَارُ, the train may be late.
Keep the strength when you translate or summarise: don't make "most likely" into "certainly".

examples.ar: مِنَ الْمُحْتَمَلِ أَنْ تَنْخَفِضَ الْأَسْعَارُ قَلِيلًا.
examples.en: Prices are likely to fall slightly.
It seems the meeting has been postponed.

examples.ar: هَذِهِ الطَّرِيقَةُ مُفِيدَةٌ إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا.
examples.en: This method is useful to some extent.

why.q_en: Why أَنْ before a verb, but أَنَّ before a noun?
why.a_en: أَنْ brings in a verb, which then ends in -a: مِنَ الْمُحْتَمَلِ أَنْ تَنْخَفِضَ. أَنَّ, with a shadda, brings in a noun, which also ends in -a: يَبْدُو أَنَّ الِاجْتِمَاعَ تَأَجَّلَ.

selftest.q_en: Which is the most certain?
selftest.why_en: The other two leave room for doubt.

selftest.q_en: What does إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا mean?
selftest.why_en: حَدّ is a limit: "up to some limit".

selftest.q_en: Which is right?
selftest.why_en: Before a noun it's أَنَّ, and the noun after it ends in -a.

lesson.arabic-implicit-meaning.title_en: What a text says and what it implies: صَرِيح, ضِمْنِيّ
lesson.arabic-implicit-meaning.family_en: Stated meaning, reasonable inference, and the small words that carry it

table.en: he suggested that, he hinted that

steps: Keep three levels apart: what the text says, صَرِيح; what it reasonably implies, ضِمْنِيّ; and what would only be a guess.
Small words often carry the implication: مَرَّةً أُخْرَى, again, implies it happened before; حَتَّى, even, implies surprise.
An implication isn't proof of someone's نِيَّة, intention: say the text suggests it, يُوحِي النَّصُّ بِأَنَّ, not that the writer meant it.
Back an interpretation with words from the text, and allow other readings when the text allows them.

examples.en: The lift broke down again.
Even the teacher didn't know the answer.
The title suggests the article is critical.

why.q_en: What does حَتَّى add in حَتَّى الْمُعَلِّمُ لَمْ يَعْرِفِ الْجَوَابَ?
why.a_en: It implies you'd expect the teacher to know. The sentence never says so; حَتَّى, even, carries that surprise.

selftest.q_en: What does مَرَّةً أُخْرَى imply in تَعَطَّلَ الْمِصْعَدُ مَرَّةً أُخْرَى?
selftest.why_en: "Again" implies an earlier time; it says nothing about who or why.

selftest.q_en: What is the opposite of صَرِيح?
selftest.why_en: صَرِيح is stated; ضِمْنِيّ is implied.

selftest.q_en: What does أَوْحَى بِأَنَّ mean?
selftest.why_en: It points to a meaning without stating it.

lesson.arabic-counterargument.title_en: Answering the other side: صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ, وَمَعَ ذَلِكَ
lesson.arabic-counterargument.family_en: Conceding a point fairly, then keeping your own
steps: Put the other view fairly, in its strongest form, before you answer it.
Concede what's true with صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ, then keep your point with مَعَ ذَلِكَ or لَكِنَّ: صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ السَّفَرَ مُكْلِفٌ، وَمَعَ ذَلِكَ فَهُوَ يُعَلِّمُ الْكَثِيرَ.
Answer the real reason, not a مُبَالَغَة, an exaggerated version of it.
Look for أَرْضِيَّةٌ مُشْتَرَكَةٌ, common ground, before you set out the difference.

examples.ar: صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ الْعَمَلَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ مُرِيحٌ، لَكِنَّهُ قَدْ يَعْزِلُ الْمُوَظَّفِينَ.
examples.en: It's true that working from home is comfortable, but it can isolate staff.

examples.ar: هَذَا اعْتِرَاضٌ وَجِيهٌ، وَمَعَ ذَلِكَ أَرَى الْأَمْرَ بِشَكْلٍ مُخْتَلِفٍ.
examples.en: That's a valid objection; even so, I see it differently.
The writer refuted the argument with figures.

why.q_en: Why الْعَمَلَ, with -a, after صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ?
why.a_en: أَنَّ, like إِنَّ, gives the noun after it -a: صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ الْعَمَلَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ مُرِيحٌ. The description keeps its -un.

selftest.q_en: Which phrase concedes a point?
selftest.why_en: مَعَ ذَلِكَ keeps your point after a concession, and فَنَّدَ is "refuted".

selftest.q_en: What does مُبَالَغَة mean?
selftest.why_en: مُبَالَغَة is from بَالَغَ, to exaggerate.

selftest.q_en: What is اِعْتِرَاضٌ وَجِيهٌ?
selftest.why_en: وَجِيه is valid, worth taking seriously.

phrases_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ السَّفَرَ مُكْلِفٌ، وَمَعَ ذَلِكَ فَهُوَ يُعَلِّمُ الْكَثِيرَ
صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ الْعَمَلَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ مُرِيحٌ

lesson.arabic-supported-debate.title_en: A structured discussion: إِذَا فَهِمْتُكَ, بِنَاءً عَلَى, أَتَفَهَّمُ
lesson.arabic-supported-debate.family_en: Taking turns, showing you've listened, and basing your point on something
steps: In a structured discussion, each turn makes a claim, gives a reason or an example, or answers what was just said.
Show you've listened by restating the other view first: إِذَا فَهِمْتُكَ جَيِّدًا, if I've understood you.
أَتَفَهَّمُ, from the same root as أَفْهَمُ, acknowledges a view without agreeing with it.
Base your point on something: بِنَاءً عَلَى, based on, a source or a clearly labelled personal example.
Wait for your دَوْر, turn. If you must interrupt, ask first: هَلْ تَسْمَحُ لِي بِمُقَاطَعَتِكَ؟

examples.ar: إِذَا فَهِمْتُكَ جَيِّدًا، فَأَنْتَ تُفَضِّلُ الدِّرَاسَةَ وَحْدَكَ.
examples.en: If I've understood you, you prefer studying on your own.

examples.ar: بِنَاءً عَلَى تَجْرِبَتِي، الْمُرَاجَعَةُ الْيَوْمِيَّةُ أَنْفَعُ.
examples.en: Based on my experience, daily revision works better.
To sum up, each method has its advantages.

why.q_en: Why أَتَفَهَّمُ, and not just أَفْهَمُ?
why.a_en: أَفْهَمُ is "I understand" the words. أَتَفَهَّمُ, from the same root, is "I understand where you're coming from": it acknowledges a view, often just before you disagree.

selftest.q_en: What is a مُقَاطَعَة?
selftest.why_en: A clarification is تَوْضِيح, and a summing-up خُلَاصَة.

selftest.q_en: What does بِنَاءً عَلَى mean?
selftest.why_en: بِنَاءً عَلَى تَجْرِبَتِي: based on my experience.

selftest.q_en: Which phrase restates the other person's view?
selftest.why_en: It checks you've understood before you answer.

lesson.arabic-word-order-agreement.title_en: Agreement and word order: وَصَلَ الْمُوَظَّفُونَ, الْمُوَظَّفُونَ وَصَلُوا
lesson.arabic-word-order-agreement.family_en: How a verb or a describing word matches a plural, depending on order and on people or things
steps: With a plural doer, word order changes the verb. Verb first, it stays singular and matches only the gender: وَصَلَ الْمُوَظَّفُونَ; وَصَلَتِ الْمُوَظَّفَاتُ.
Doer first, the verb matches in number too: الْمُوَظَّفُونَ وَصَلُوا; الْمُوَظَّفَاتُ وَصَلْنَ.
Plurals of things and animals, not people, are treated as feminine singular: الْكُتُبُ جَدِيدَةٌ, the books are new; الْكُتُبُ وَصَلَتْ, the books arrived.

In a sentence with no verb, the describing word follows the same rules: with people it matches the مُبْتَدَأ, the subject, in gender and number, الْمُوَظَّفُونَ مُجْتَهِدُونَ; with things it is feminine singular, الْكُتُبُ جَدِيدَةٌ.

examples.en: The (women) students arrived early.
The engineers work in the factory.
These questions are difficult.

why.q_en: Why الْكُتُبُ جَدِيدَةٌ, feminine singular, when كِتَاب is masculine?
why.a_en: Plurals of things and animals, not people, are treated as feminine singular, whatever the singular's gender: الْكُتُبُ جَدِيدَةٌ, هَذِهِ الْأَسْئِلَةُ. Plurals of people follow the people: الْمُهَنْدِسُونَ مُجْتَهِدُونَ.

selftest.q_en: Which is right, with the doer first?
selftest.why_en: With the doer first, the verb is plural too.

selftest.q_en: Which is right for "the questions are easy"?
selftest.why_en: A plural of things takes the feminine singular.

selftest.q_en: Verb first: "The (women) nurses arrived"?
selftest.why_en: Verb first, it stays singular and matches only the gender.

lesson.arabic-hal-tamyiz.title_en: Two kinds of -an that aren't objects: the حَال and the تَمْيِيز
lesson.arabic-hal-tamyiz.family_en: A word that says what state someone was in, and a word that says what is meant or counted

table.en: the weather got colder (literally "increased in coldness")

steps: Two common kinds of word end in -an without being an object: the حَال, which says what state someone was in, and the تَمْيِيز, which says what is meant or counted.
A حَال answers "in what state?": رَجَعَ سَامِي مُبْتَسِمًا, Sāmī came back smiling. It matches the person: دَخَلَتِ الْمُدِيرَةُ غَاضِبَةً.
A تَمْيِيز answers "of what?" or "in what respect?": after 11 to 99, خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ قَلَمًا; after a comparison, أَكْثَرُ خِبْرَةً, more experienced.
Ask what question the word answers before you name it.

examples.en: The manager came into the room angry.

examples.ar: هَذَا الْفُنْدُقُ أَفْضَلُ مَوْقِعًا مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْفُنْدُقِ.
examples.en: This hotel is better located than that one.
The players came back onto the pitch at a run.

why.q_en: How do I tell a حَال from a تَمْيِيز when both end in -an?
why.a_en: Ask what it answers. "In what state was someone?" makes it a حَال: مُبْتَسِمًا. "Of what?" or "in what respect?" makes it a تَمْيِيز: قَلَمًا after a number, مَوْقِعًا after أَفْضَلُ.

selftest.q_en: Which word is a تَمْيِيز?
selftest.why_en: It says what is counted. مُبْتَسِمًا is a حَال, and الْغُرْفَةَ an object.

selftest.q_en: How do you say "The girl came in smiling"?
selftest.why_en: A حَال matches the person, a girl, and ends in -an.

selftest.q_en: What does أَكْثَرُ خِبْرَةً mean?
selftest.why_en: خِبْرَةً says in what respect: "more in experience".

lesson.arabic-numbers-exceptions.title_en: Numbers past ten, and words that never take tanween
lesson.arabic-numbers-exceptions.family_en: 11 to 19, the tens, a hundred and a thousand, and the مَمْنُوعٌ مِنَ الصَّرْفِ
steps: From 11 to 19, both parts of the number end in -a, except the first part of 12, which changes like a word for two: اِثْنَا عَشَرَ, اِثْنَيْ عَشَرَ. The noun after them is singular with -an: خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا.
In 13 to 19, the first part takes the opposite gender, as 3 to 10 do, while عَشَرَ or عَشْرَةَ matches the noun: خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَاعَةً. In 11 and 12, both parts match: أَحَدَ عَشَرَ شَهْرًا.
The tens, from عِشْرُونَ to تِسْعُونَ, also take a singular noun with -an: عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا.
مِئَة and أَلْف take a singular noun ending in -i: مِئَةُ سَنَةٍ, أَلْفُ كِتَابٍ.

Some words never take tanween: the مَمْنُوعٌ مِنَ الصَّرْفِ, like مَدَارِس. On their own they end in -a where other words end in -i: فِي مَدَارِسَ. With الْـ, or as the first word of an إِضَافَة, the -i comes back: فِي الْمَدَارِسِ, فِي مَدَارِسِ الْمَدِينَةِ.

examples.ar: قَضَيْتُ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا فِي الْقَرْيَةِ.
examples.en: I spent fifteen days in the village.

examples.ar: حَضَرَ الْمُحَاضَرَةَ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ مِئَةِ طَالِبٍ.
examples.en: More than a hundred students came to the lecture.
We visited many cities and old museums.

why.q_en: Why مَتَاحِفَ, with no -an, next to مُدُنًا?
why.a_en: مَتَاحِف is one of the words that never take tanween: plurals shaped like مَدَارِس and مَتَاحِف are among them. Where مُدُنًا has -an, مَتَاحِفَ has a plain -a.

selftest.q_en: Which is right for "fifteen hours"?
selftest.why_en: سَاعَة is feminine: the first part has no ـَة, عَشْرَةَ matches, and the noun is singular.

selftest.q_en: Which is right for "a thousand books"?
selftest.why_en: After أَلْف, the noun is singular and ends in -in.

selftest.q_en: Which never takes tanween?
selftest.why_en: Plurals shaped like مَدَارِس are مَمْنُوعٌ مِنَ الصَّرْفِ. مَدْرَسَةٌ and طُلَّابٌ take tanween.

lesson.arabic-negation-exception.title_en: Only, except and nobody: إِلَّا, إِنَّمَا, فَقَطْ, لَا أَحَدَ
lesson.arabic-negation-exception.family_en: How far a negative reaches, and the words that restrict or except

table.en: the problem is only the time

steps: A negative followed by إِلَّا means "only": مَا بَقِيَ إِلَّا يَوْمَانِ, only two days are left. It doesn't mean that none are left.
With no negative before it, إِلَّا means "except": حَضَرَ الْجَمِيعُ إِلَّا لَيْلَى, everyone came except Laylā.
لَا before a noun with a plain -a means "no … at all": لَا أَحَدَ, nobody; لَا شَكَّ, no doubt.
إِنَّمَا restricts the sentence to its last part: إِنَّمَا الْمُشْكِلَةُ فِي الْوَقْتِ, the problem is only in the time. فَقَطْ, only, comes after the word it limits.
Check how far a negative reaches: لَمْ يَحْضُرِ الْجَمِيعُ, not everyone came, isn't لَمْ يَحْضُرْ أَحَدٌ, nobody came.

examples.ar: لَمْ يَحْضُرِ الْجَمِيعُ، بَلْ نِصْفُهُمْ فَقَطْ.
examples.en: Not everyone came: only half of them.
Nobody knows the answer.

examples.ar: مَا بَقِيَ إِلَّا يَوْمَانِ عَلَى الِامْتِحَانِ.
examples.en: Only two days are left until the exam.

why.q_en: Why يَوْمَانِ, with -āni, in مَا بَقِيَ إِلَّا يَوْمَانِ?
why.a_en: When a negative sentence has nothing before إِلَّا for it to except from, the word after إِلَّا takes the ending its role needs. Here the two days are what's left, the subject of بَقِيَ, so -āni.

selftest.q_en: What does مَا بَقِيَ إِلَّا يَوْمَانِ mean?
selftest.why_en: A negative with إِلَّا restricts; it doesn't deny.

selftest.q_en: Which says "nobody"?
selftest.why_en: لَا with a plain -a: no one at all.

selftest.q_en: What does حَضَرَ الْجَمِيعُ إِلَّا لَيْلَى mean?
selftest.why_en: With no negative before it, إِلَّا is "except".

lesson.arabic-precision-edit.title_en: Editing for precision: the meaning before the polish
lesson.arabic-precision-edit.family_en: What to check first, the small words that change a claim, and the words for editing
steps: Edit for meaning first: who did it, when, whether it's negative, how many, who "he" is, and how sure.
A smooth sentence is still wrong if it changes the claim: قَدْ يُفْتَحُ غَدًا, it may open tomorrow, isn't فُتِحَ أَمْسِ, it opened yesterday.
Watch the small words that carry a lot: a dropped لَا or لَمْ reverses a sentence, and a dropped قَدْ turns "may" into "does".
Then check the grammar where it matters: agreement, endings after small words, and spelling.
Where a word is unclear, suggest a بَدِيل, an alternative, and keep the original meaning بِأَمَانَةٍ, faithfully.

examples.ar: حُذِفَتْ أَدَاةُ النَّفْيِ سَهْوًا، فَانْقَلَبَ الْمَعْنَى.
examples.en: The negative particle was deleted by mistake, so the meaning was reversed.

examples.ar: هَذِهِ الصِّيغَةُ أَوْضَحُ، لَكِنَّهَا تُغَيِّرُ الْمَعْنَى.
examples.en: This wording is clearer, but it changes the meaning.

examples.ar: نَقَلْتُ الْمَعْنَى بِأَمَانَةٍ دُونَ أَيِّ زِيَادَةٍ.
examples.en: I conveyed the meaning faithfully, without adding anything.

why.q_en: Why حُذِفَتْ, with u and i, in حُذِفَتْ أَدَاةُ النَّفْيِ?
why.a_en: It's the passive: حَذَفَ, he deleted; حُذِفَ, it was deleted, with no one named. The ـَتْ matches أَدَاة, which is feminine.

selftest.q_en: What does سَهْوًا mean?
selftest.why_en: "On purpose" is عَمْدًا.

selftest.q_en: Which change alters the claim, not just the style?
choices: swapping a word for a synonym
selftest.why_en: Losing a negative reverses the meaning.

selftest.q_en: What is غُمُوض?
selftest.why_en: An alternative is بَدِيل, and a deletion حَذْف.

lesson.arabic-essay-architecture.title_en: Planning an essay: أُطْرُوحَة, مِحْوَر, اِسْتِنْتَاج
lesson.arabic-essay-architecture.family_en: A position, sections that each do one job, a fair counterargument, and a conclusion that follows
steps: An essay answers a question with a position, its أُطْرُوحَة, and organised reasons for it.
Plan before drafting: a مُخَطَّط that gives each paragraph one job, such as a reason, its evidence and its limit.
Put the sections in a clear تَسَلْسُل, order, and introduce each: يَتَنَاوَلُ الْمِحْوَرُ الثَّانِي, the second section deals with.
Give the strongest حُجَّةٌ مُضَادَّةٌ, counterargument, a fair hearing, then answer it.
The conclusion draws together what you've argued; it doesn't bring in a new claim.

examples.en: The first section deals with the cost of studying.

examples.ar: تَدْعُو هَذِهِ الْمَقَالَةُ إِلَى التَّعَلُّمِ الذَّاتِيِّ بِشُرُوطٍ.
examples.en: This essay argues for self-study, under certain conditions.
From the above, we conclude that follow-up is essential.

why.q_en: Why مِمَّا, and not مِنْ مَا?
why.a_en: مِنْ and مَا join in writing, and the ن merges into the م: مِمَّا, from what. مِمَّا سَبَقَ, from what came before, is a common way into a conclusion.

selftest.q_en: What is a مُخَطَّط?
selftest.why_en: A conclusion is اِسْتِنْتَاج.

selftest.q_en: What is an essay's أُطْرُوحَة?
selftest.why_en: It's what the essay argues for.

selftest.q_en: How is "from what" written?
selftest.why_en: The ن merges into the م, which takes a shadda.

lesson.arabic-presentation-design.title_en: Giving a presentation: signposting the route
lesson.arabic-presentation-design.family_en: Fitting a talk to its audience and time, and the phrases that move it along
steps: Fit the talk to its جُمْهُور, audience, and its time: an opening, a few connected points, one concrete example.
Tell the audience the route at the start: سَأَبْدَأُ بِالْمُشْكِلَةِ، ثُمَّ أَعْرِضُ الْحَلَّ, I'll start with the problem, then present the solution.
Signal each move: أَنْتَقِلُ الْآنَ إِلَى, I'll move on now to; وَأَخِيرًا, and finally.
Keep your notes to cue words, not a script, and watch your وَتِيرَة, pace.
Slides support the talk; they can't make up for unclear speech. Leave time for questions.

examples.en: I'll start with the problem, then present the solution.
I'll move on now to the next slide.
We have ten minutes for questions.

why.q_en: Why is a presentation عَرْض, and "I present" أَعْرِضُ?
why.a_en: They share the root ع-ر-ض, about showing: عَرَضَ, to show or present, with its present يَعْرِضُ, so "I present" is أَعْرِضُ; عَرْض is the showing itself, a presentation.

selftest.q_en: What is a شَرِيحَة in a presentation?
selftest.why_en: Slides support the talk; they don't replace it.

selftest.q_en: Which phrase moves on to the next point?
selftest.why_en: سَأَبْدَأُ بِالْمُشْكِلَةِ opens the talk.

selftest.q_en: What is وَتِيرَة?
selftest.why_en: The length of a talk is its مُدَّة.

lesson.arabic-qa-spontaneity.title_en: Answering questions: أَفْهَمُ مِنْ كَلَامِكَ أَنَّ, أَعْتَرِفُ بِأَنَّ
lesson.arabic-qa-spontaneity.family_en: Checking what's asked, admitting what you don't know, and keeping to the question

table.en: I understand from what you say that
outside the scope of the study

steps: Work out what kind of question it is: about meaning, about evidence, or about scope. Then answer that one.
If it's unclear, check what you've understood: أَفْهَمُ مِنْ كَلَامِكَ أَنَّ, I understand from what you say that.
Say plainly what you don't know, and mark a guess as a تَخْمِين, a guess.
If the question goes beyond what you covered, say so: هَذَا خَارِجَ نِطَاقِ الْبَحْثِ, that's outside the scope of the study.
A short, qualified answer beats a long answer to a different question.

examples.ar: أَفْهَمُ مِنْ كَلَامِكَ أَنَّ التَّكْلِفَةَ هِيَ الْمُشْكِلَةُ.
examples.en: I understand from what you say that cost is the problem.

examples.ar: هَذَا مُجَرَّدُ تَخْمِينٍ، وَلَيْسَ نَتِيجَةً مُؤَكَّدَةً.
examples.en: That's only a guess, not a confirmed result.
I admit that the sample was small.

why.q_en: Why أَعْتَرِفُ بِأَنَّ, with بِـ before أَنَّ?
why.a_en: اِعْتَرَفَ, to admit, takes بِـ before what you admit: أَعْتَرِفُ بِالْخَطَأِ, I admit the mistake. Before a whole statement, بِـ joins أَنَّ: أَعْتَرِفُ بِأَنَّ الْعَيِّنَةَ كَانَتْ صَغِيرَةً.

selftest.q_en: What does بِالضَّبْطِ mean?
selftest.why_en: "Roughly" is تَقْرِيبًا.

selftest.q_en: What is a تَخْمِين?
selftest.why_en: Mark a guess as one, so it isn't taken for a finding.

selftest.q_en: Which phrase checks you've understood the question?
selftest.why_en: It restates the question before you answer.

lesson.arabic-register-adaptation.title_en: Adapting to your audience: مُصْطَلَح, بِعِبَارَةٍ أَبْسَطَ
lesson.arabic-register-adaptation.family_en: Keeping the facts while changing the words for a specialist or a beginner
steps: Register is who you're talking to, and why. A مُتَخَصِّص, specialist, can take the terms; a مُبْتَدِئ, beginner, needs them explained.
To simplify, define the term or swap it for familiar words: بِعِبَارَةٍ أَبْسَطَ, in simpler words, or أَيْ, that is.
Simple doesn't mean colloquial: plain Standard Arabic works for everyone.
Keep the facts and the limits: a simpler sentence mustn't drop a "may" or an "only".
Formal doesn't mean complicated: short sentences with clear links are still formal.

examples.ar: التَّشْفِيرُ يَحْمِي الْبَيَانَاتِ، أَيْ إِنَّهُ يَمْنَعُ غَيْرَكَ مِنْ قِرَاءَتِهَا.
examples.en: Encryption protects data; that is, it stops others from reading it.

examples.ar: بِعِبَارَةٍ أَبْسَطَ، الْبَرْنَامَجُ يَحْفَظُ نُسْخَةً مِنْ عَمَلِكَ.
examples.en: In simpler words, the program keeps a copy of your work.
The teacher simplified the explanation for beginners.

why.q_en: Why أَبْسَطَ, with -a, after بِعِبَارَةٍ?
why.a_en: أَبْسَط, simpler, is a comparative on the أَفْعَل pattern, like أَكْبَر and أَفْضَل. These comparatives never take tanween, so where another describing word would end in -in after بِعِبَارَةٍ, this one ends in -a: بِعِبَارَةٍ أَبْسَطَ.

selftest.q_en: What is a مُصْطَلَح?
selftest.why_en: A مُصْطَلَح is a word with a fixed meaning in one field; a style is أُسْلُوب.

selftest.q_en: What does بَسَّطَ mean?
selftest.why_en: بَسَّطَ comes from بَسِيط, simple.

selftest.q_en: What is a مُبْتَدِئ?
selftest.why_en: A specialist is مُتَخَصِّص.

lesson.arabic-b2-output-review.title_en: Reviewing your work by criteria: وُضُوح, تَمَاسُك, دِقَّة, طَلَاقَة
lesson.arabic-b2-output-review.family_en: The words for what makes speaking and writing work, and how to use them on your own output
steps: Review your work against several criteria, not one overall impression.
وُضُوح, clarity: can the listener follow? تَمَاسُك, cohesion: do the parts hold together? دِقَّة, accuracy: are the forms right? طَلَاقَة, fluency: does it flow?
One strong feature can hide a weak one: a fluent talk can still have unclear references.
Look for the patterns that keep coming back, and pick one or two for your next task.

examples.ar: كَانَ الْعَرْضُ وَاضِحًا، لَكِنَّ الْمُتَحَدِّثَ أَسْرَعَ قَلِيلًا.
examples.en: The presentation was clear, but the speaker went a little fast.

examples.ar: تَحْتَاجُ الْمَقَالَةُ إِلَى مَزِيدٍ مِنَ التَّمَاسُكِ بَيْنَ الْفِقْرَاتِ.
examples.en: The essay needs more cohesion between its paragraphs.
His vocabulary is wide, and his accuracy is good.

why.q_en: What's the difference between وُضُوح and دِقَّة?
why.a_en: وُضُوح is whether the meaning gets across; دِقَّة is whether the forms are right. A text can be clear with a few errors in it, or accurate and still hard to follow.

selftest.q_en: What is طَلَاقَة?
selftest.why_en: Accuracy is دِقَّة, and clarity وُضُوح.

selftest.q_en: Which word means "cohesion"?
selftest.why_en: A criterion is مِعْيَار.

selftest.q_en: What is ثَرْوَةٌ لُغَوِيَّةٌ?
selftest.why_en: Literally "linguistic wealth".

lesson.arabic-b2-listening-reading.title_en: Following a long text or talk: its point, its asides, its reservations
lesson.arabic-b2-listening-reading.family_en: Telling narration from judgement, and keeping the limits a writer puts on a claim
steps: A long text mixes kinds of passage: سَرْد, telling what happened; description; and حُكْم, the writer's judgement. Notice which is which as you go.
Find مَغْزَى الْكَلَامِ, the point, and don't mistake an اِسْتِطْرَاد, an aside, for it.
Keep every تَحَفُّظ, every reservation: words like إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا, to some extent, or فِي بَعْضِ الْحَالَاتِ, in some cases, limit the claim.
Listen first without the تَفْرِيغ, the transcript; use it afterwards to check, and note that you did.

examples.ar: يَسْرُدُ الْكَاتِبُ أَحْدَاثَ الرِّحْلَةِ، ثُمَّ يُصْدِرُ حُكْمَهُ عَلَيْهَا.
examples.en: The writer narrates the events of the trip, then gives his judgement on it.

examples.ar: وَهَذَا اسْتِطْرَادٌ لَا عَلَاقَةَ لَهُ بِالْمَوْضُوعِ.
examples.en: And this is an aside with nothing to do with the topic.

examples.ar: يُوَافِقُ الْمُتَحَدِّثُ عَلَى الْفِكْرَةِ مَعَ بَعْضِ التَّحَفُّظَاتِ.
examples.en: The speaker agrees with the idea, with some reservations.

why.q_en: What's the difference between سَرْد and حُكْم?
why.a_en: سَرْد tells what happened, in order; حُكْم is the writer's view of it. A summary keeps them apart: what the text reports, and what the writer thinks of it.

selftest.q_en: What is مَغْزَى الْكَلَامِ?
selftest.why_en: An aside is اِسْتِطْرَاد.

selftest.q_en: What is the تَفْرِيغ of a recording?
selftest.why_en: It's the recording written out word for word.

selftest.q_en: What does مَعَ بَعْضِ التَّحَفُّظَاتِ add to "he agrees"?
selftest.why_en: It limits the agreement; keep it in a summary.

lesson.arabic-b2-unseen-output.title_en: An unseen task: reading its conditions, and speaking off the cuff
lesson.arabic-b2-unseen-output.family_en: The words for a task's limits, and how to plan fast for a prompt you haven't seen
steps: An unseen task tests what you can do with a new prompt. Read its conditions first: عَدَدُ الْكَلِمَاتِ, the word count; any حَدٌّ أَقْصَى, maximum; the time allowed.
Plan quickly: name your audience, take a position, answer one counterargument, and limit any claim you can't support.
Expect follow-up questions you haven't seen, and answer them اِرْتِجَالًا, off the cuff.
Keep النُّسْخَةُ الْأُولَى, the first version, as it was, and label each later تَعْدِيل, revision, with the help you had.

examples.ar: لَا يَزِيدُ النَّصُّ عَلَى ثَلَاثِمِئَةِ كَلِمَةٍ.
examples.en: The text is no more than three hundred words.

examples.ar: تَكَلَّمَتْ سَلْمَى ارْتِجَالًا لِمُدَّةِ خَمْسِ دَقَائِقَ.
examples.en: Salmā spoke off the cuff for five minutes.

examples.ar: أَرْسَلْتُ النُّسْخَةَ الْأُولَى قَبْلَ أَيِّ تَعْدِيلٍ.
examples.en: I sent the first version before any revision.

why.q_en: Why ثَلَاثِمِئَةِ كَلِمَةٍ, with كَلِمَة singular?
why.a_en: After مِئَة, and after three hundred, four hundred and the rest, the noun is singular and ends in -in, as after أَلْف: ثَلَاثُمِئَةِ كَلِمَةٍ, three hundred words. Only the first part changes its ending with its job in the sentence: عَلَى ثَلَاثِمِئَةِ كَلِمَةٍ.

selftest.q_en: What does اِرْتِجَالًا mean?
selftest.why_en: Answering live questions means speaking this way.

selftest.q_en: What is عَدَدُ الْكَلِمَاتِ?
selftest.why_en: It's one of the conditions to read first.

selftest.q_en: Which is right for "five hundred words"?
selftest.why_en: After the hundreds, the noun is singular and ends in -in.

lesson.arabic-portfolio-audit.title_en: Claims about your ability, with evidence: عَيِّنَة, قُدْرَة
lesson.arabic-portfolio-audit.family_en: Matching what you say you can do to dated, varied samples
steps: Say exactly what you can do: أَسْتَطِيعُ فَهْمَ نَشَرَاتِ الْأَخْبَارِ الْقَصِيرَةِ بِدُونِ تَرْجَمَةٍ, I can understand short news bulletins without translation.
Back each claim with an عَيِّنَة, a sample: the task, its date, and the help you had.
Check that the samples are recent and مُتَنَوِّع, varied, and that some were done on your own.
A revised translation, a practised talk and an unseen listening task show different abilities: say which is which.

examples.ar: أَضَفْتُ إِلَى مِلَفِّي عَيِّنَةً مِنْ كِتَابَتِي الْأَخِيرَةِ.
examples.en: I added a sample of my recent writing to my file.

examples.ar: تُظْهِرُ هَذِهِ الْعَيِّنَةُ قُدْرَتِي عَلَى الْمُنَاقَشَةِ.
examples.en: This sample shows my ability to discuss.

examples.ar: وَصَفْتُ مُسْتَوَايَ بِدِقَّةٍ فِي سِيرَتِي الذَّاتِيَّةِ.
examples.en: I described my level accurately in my CV.

why.q_en: Why قُدْرَتِي عَلَى الْمُنَاقَشَةِ, with عَلَى?
why.a_en: قُدْرَة, ability, takes عَلَى, like قَادِر, able: قُدْرَتِي عَلَى الْمُنَاقَشَةِ, my ability to discuss. What follows is usually a verbal noun, or أَنْ with a verb: قُدْرَتِي عَلَى أَنْ أُنَاقِشَ.

selftest.q_en: What is an عَيِّنَة?
selftest.why_en: Note the shadda: عَيِّنَة, a sample; the plural is عَيِّنَات.

selftest.q_en: What is a سِيرَةٌ ذَاتِيَّةٌ?
selftest.why_en: Literally "one's own life story".

selftest.q_en: How do you say "my ability to write"?
selftest.why_en: قُدْرَة takes عَلَى; after it comes a verbal noun, or أَنْ with a verb.

phrases_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ فَهْمَ نَشَرَاتِ الْأَخْبَارِ الْقَصِيرَةِ بِدُونِ تَرْجَمَةٍ

lesson.arabic-external-assessment.title_en: Feedback from outside: تَغْذِيَةٌ رَاجِعَةٌ, اِمْتِحَانٌ رَسْمِيٌّ
lesson.arabic-external-assessment.family_en: The words for tutors, exams and fees, and what each kind of assessment shows
steps: Outside feedback catches what self-study misses. Decide what you need first: a tutor's تَغْذِيَةٌ رَاجِعَةٌ, a fresh sample marked by someone else, or an اِمْتِحَانٌ رَسْمِيٌّ, an official exam.
Before paying any رُسُوم, fees, check which skills and which kind of Arabic the service assesses.
A مُدَرِّسٌ خُصُوصِيٌّ, a private tutor, can ask you follow-up questions; a written test can't.
A result covers what was tested, and no more.

examples.ar: حَصَلْتُ عَلَى تَغْذِيَةٍ رَاجِعَةٍ مُفِيدَةٍ مِنْ مُدَرِّسِي.
examples.en: I got useful feedback from my tutor.

examples.ar: يُقَيِّمُ هَذَا الِامْتِحَانُ الْقِرَاءَةَ وَالْكِتَابَةَ فَقَطْ.
examples.en: This exam assesses reading and writing only.
Is this certificate accredited?

why.q_en: Why تَغْذِيَةٌ رَاجِعَةٌ, literally "returning nourishment", for feedback?
why.a_en: It's a word-for-word rendering of the English: تَغْذِيَة, feeding, and رَاجِعَة, coming back. The phrase is fixed, and both words take their endings together: حَصَلْتُ عَلَى تَغْذِيَةٍ رَاجِعَةٍ.

selftest.q_en: What is a مُدَرِّسٌ خُصُوصِيٌّ?
selftest.why_en: خُصُوصِيّ is private, personal.

selftest.q_en: What does مُعْتَمَد mean for a certificate?
selftest.why_en: From اِعْتَمَدَ, to approve, to rely on.

selftest.q_en: What are رُسُوم?
selftest.why_en: رُسُومُ التَّسْجِيلِ are registration fees.

lesson.arabic-lifelong-plan.title_en: Keeping your Arabic going: مَجَال, حَافَظَ عَلَى, دَوْرِيًّا
lesson.arabic-lifelong-plan.family_en: A field to grow in, the common skills to keep up, and a pace you can sustain
steps: Pick a مَجَال, a field, because it serves a real purpose, and keep up general reading, listening, speaking and writing alongside it.
حَافَظَ عَلَى, to keep up, takes عَلَى: أُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْقِرَاءَةِ الْيَوْمِيَّةِ, I keep up daily reading.
Test yourself دَوْرِيًّا, regularly, on something unfamiliar, and keep getting feedback.
Fit the عِبْءُ الْعَمَلِ, the workload, to your time and energy. After an اِنْقِطَاع, a break, check where you are and refresh what you need.

examples.ar: أُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْقِرَاءَةِ الْأَدَبِيَّةِ إِلَى جَانِبِ تَخَصُّصِي.
examples.en: I keep up literary reading alongside my specialism.
After a long break, I revised the basics.

examples.ar: هَدَفِي عَلَى الْمَدَى الْبَعِيدِ قِرَاءَةُ الصُّحُفِ بِسُهُولَةٍ.
examples.en: My long-term goal is reading newspapers with ease.

why.q_en: Why أُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْقِرَاءَةِ, and not أُحَافِظُ الْقِرَاءَةَ?
why.a_en: حَافَظَ, to keep up or preserve, takes عَلَى before what you keep: أُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْقِرَاءَةِ. Learn it with its partner, as with اِعْتَمَدَ عَلَى, to depend on.

selftest.q_en: What does دَوْرِيًّا mean?
selftest.why_en: From دَوْر, a turn or a cycle.

selftest.q_en: What is عِبْءُ الْعَمَلِ?
selftest.why_en: عِبْء is a load, a burden.

selftest.q_en: Which is right for "I keep up my listening"?
selftest.why_en: حَافَظَ takes عَلَى.
